subject: Issues with using advanced sleep log in study with shift workers

messages.author: 0ea0951b75e71d9a
messages.subject: Issues with using advanced sleep log in study with shift workers
parts:
Hi Vincent,

I am new to using GGIR, and have run into a few issues that I was hoping you could provide some advice on. Briefly, we are studying shift workers that:
(1) often have multiple sleeps per day,
(2) don't all start the study on the same calendar date

I've been trying to work through using a basic sleep log and an advanced sleep log, but both options have some issues below:
With the basic sleep log: we are unable to use this as it only accepts one sleep period per day

With the advanced sleep log:
(1) because some participants sleep 2 or 3 times per day, we have the problem of defining which is a "sleep" and which are "naps", particularly when participants have all sleep episodes between 8am-8pm (if they are on night shifts). I was wondering what your advice would be?
(2) the advanced sleep log requires a date, which is typically the date of wake. However, if they are napping between 12pm-1pm, would I still enter in the date of wake, and GGIR is able to work out that sleep onset is 12pm on the same day (and not the day before?)?
(3) The final issue is that participants begin the study on different dates. Would you recommend setting N1 as the first date of the first participant, and the later participants will start on N3 or N4, with the corresponding date of wake listed in the sleep log?

Our sleep logs are electronic and stored in long format. It became very complex and difficult to set up codes that are capable of incorporating all the above considerations and reshape teh format into the "wide" format that GGIR requires.


Looking forward to hearing from you, and thank you so much in advance,
Lin
